abstract.para: The Apache HTTP Server (Apache) is a feature-rich, open source Web server. In &suselinux; &productnumber;, Apache follows the stable lifecycle model. This model balances the delivery of security fixes and other relevant upstream changes with the compatibility and long-term stability expected from &suselinux; systems.

section.title: Upstream compatibility policy
section.para: The Apache HTTP Server Project maintains stable release branches, identified by even-numbered minor versions. Within a stable branch, upstream designs revisions to remain compatible to the maximum possible extent. This applies to the module API, the runtime configuration and the compile-time configuration (the configure options supported by one revision remain supported by later ones). Features may be added, and features may be deprecated with appropriate documentation. This compatibility-oriented policy is what allows &suse; to update Apache regularly during General Availability (GA) without introducing disruptive changes.

note.para: Upstream compatibility does not constitute an unconditional guarantee for every third-party module, local customization or deployment configuration. Verify new Apache package versions with your particular configuration and module set before deploying updates in production.

section.title: Update strategy and lifecycle model
section.para: For Apache in &suselinux; &productnumber;, &suse; maintains the stable update strategy, which combines a rolling-style update approach during GA with a more conservative approach during LTS.

listitem.para: For &suselinux; minor releases in GA, the Apache package is upgraded when a new upstream Apache version is released. New upstream versions are typically released several times per year.

When a &suselinux; minor release enters LTS, the Apache version is frozen. Version upgrades are avoided during LTS unless they are considered necessary. Potential version upgrades are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, taking into account security, maintenance and compatibility requirements.

section.para: The LTS freeze does not prevent an exceptional version update when one is required. In particular, &suse; retains the option of performing an emergency version update when necessary to address a critical security vulnerability or other exceptional requirement.
